transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marcus Lee, Priya Nair; Carlos Mendes, Aisha Khan, Tom Baker, Maya Li

[00:00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, can you hear me ok?
[00:00:05] Carlos Mendes: yes, loud and clear.
[00:00:07] Aisha Khan: yep good here.
[00:00:10] Lena Park: awesome. agenda — quick run through the benchmark deltas vs your baseline provider, then tuning knobs we tried this week, and then action items. Marcus will start with the numbers.
[00:00:24] Marcus Lee: cool thanks lena. so we ran the same workload you sent — approx 300 concurrent users simulated, average request size ~120 tokens, 99th-percentile seq length around 512. baseline provider results are in the sheet under column 'baseline' and our runs are 'redwood-v1' and 'redwood-quant4'.
[00:00:45] Marcus Lee: high-level: for the float32 run (redwood-v1) p50 was 72ms, p95 180ms, p99 ~420ms at target qps of 1200. baseline had p50 130ms, p95 330ms, p99 780ms on same infra. so we see a meaningful tail improvement, particularly around the p99.
[00:01:10] Tom Baker: sorry real quick — are those numbers end-to-end with your gateway, or just token generation time? we need the E2E number for SLAs.
[00:01:18] Marcus Lee: good call — these are end-to-end including our ingress, routing, and small post-processing. for clarity, raw model token latency p50 is ~45ms in our run.
[00:01:29] Aisha Khan: ok that’s promising. what about throughput — can you push higher than 1200 qps?
[00:01:35] Marcus Lee: we tested up to 2k qps with autoscaling on dedicated pools. throughput plateaued around 2.6k sustained for 30s bursts before queuing increased. baseline plateaued earlier around 1.8k.
[00:01:50] Marcus Lee: important caveat — we used continuous batching and a 64ms batching window which improves token utilization. if you reduce latency SLO we can shrink that window.
[00:02:02] Carlos Mendes: batching window 64ms — that’s the default? does that add to p50?
[00:02:06] Marcus Lee: it can add a few ms to p50 for low QPS traffic, but for your traffic pattern it actually reduces tail because it avoids cold starts and packs requests better. we also tested prefix (KV) caching for repeated contexts and saw ~30% token compute reduction for common prefixes.
[00:02:20] Maya Li: quick question about quantization — you tried 4-bit quant? how did quality look for our evaluation prompts?
[00:02:27] Marcus Lee: yes redwood-quant4 was the 4-bit run. p50 dropped to 58ms, p95 150ms, p99 360ms. throughput improved ~20%. in terms of quality we ran your 150 prompt eval set — automated metrics (ROUGE/EM-like heuristics) showed <1.5% delta on average but there were a couple of edge cases where factuality drifted slightly. we flagged those examples in the sheet.
[00:02:50] Aisha Khan: hmm we'll need to review flagged examples. for production we have strict quality thresholds on those templates.
[00:02:55] Lena Park: totally. we can run a focused eval and also try mixed precision where critical prompts go to float and others to quant4. that’s a routing rule we can do in the runtime.
[00:03:07] Tom Baker: SLA question — if we go dedicated, are you able to guarantee tail latency? we need 99.9% under 1s for external customers.
[00:03:16] Priya Nair: short answer yes — with dedicated pools and our autoscaling/fallback policies we can hit 99.9% under 1s for the workload profile you provided. we'll include an SLA draft in the follow-up.
[00:03:26] Carlos Mendes: great. another question — what about encryption and audit logs? we need KMS integration and immutable audit trails.
[00:03:32] Priya Nair: we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS (AWS KMS or customer HSM) for private deployments and produce audit logs for every request with token-level breakdowns. I'll attach the SOC2/ISO compliance doc in the follow-up.
[00:03:44] Marcus Lee: back to benchmarks — we also profiled kernel utilization. on Ampere A100-like nodes baseline had more memory stalls; our runtime uses a different KV cache layout and reduces GPU memory churn which helps tail latency. some of the notes have mildly incorrect transcriptions in the automated profiler export — you might see 'K V cash' spelled weirdly, sorry about that.
[00:04:05] Aisha Khan: ha yes i noticed that in the csv. not a problem.
[00:04:08] Marcus Lee: we also tested a scenario with per-request function/tool calls (your external lookup). that added ~35ms average but baseline added ~90ms due to extra hops. so integration pattern matters.
[00:04:20] Lena Park: sounds like the net is favorable for Redwood on latency and throughput for this workload, but we should validate E2E on your staging. next up — tuning knobs we recommend for the pilot. Marcus?
[00:04:32] Marcus Lee: recommended tuning: 1) enable prefix KV cache for repeat contexts, 2) start with quant4 but route critical templates to float, 3) set batching window to 32ms for low-latency routes and 64ms for high-throughput routes, 4) use a dedicated pool with burst capacity enabled.
[00:04:50] Carlos Mendes: what about warm-up — do you need pre-populated KV caches?
[00:04:54] Marcus Lee: ideally yes. we can seed caches with common prefixes from your logs and run a short warm-up traffic replay. that reduced p99 by ~12% in our runs.
[00:05:03] Tom Baker: replay — we'll share a 10-minute trace from staging. should be fine.
[00:05:07] Lena Park: perfect. pricing — Lena: can you give a quick sketch of cost difference if we go dedicated vs hosted?
[00:05:14] Lena Park: yes. ballpark — hosted usage-based at your projected 200k tokens/day is approximately $X/day (we'll send exact numbers), dedicated monthly commit gives ~30% lower unit cost but requires a baseline commit. i'll send a delta spreadsheet.
[00:05:28] Carlos Mendes: ok want to see the commit math.
[00:05:30] Aisha Khan: also can you show the accuracy regressions per prompt for quant4 — put that in the flagged tab.
[00:05:35] Marcus Lee: already did, see 'quant4-flagged-examples' tab, but we'll add comments and suggested prompt workarounds.
[00:05:43] Maya Li: curious — did you compare against ProviderX's latest optimized run?
[00:05:48] Marcus Lee: we have a ProviderX column; their latency was better on p50 sometimes but tail was worse. also they lacked the same prefix caching behavior we used. note that provider names can be transcribed oddly in our auto export.
[00:06:02] Lena Park: ok next — reliability: any errors or OOMs in the runs?
[00:06:06] Marcus Lee: no OOMs. error rate was <0.1% across runs, similar to baseline. we saw a couple of transient 503s during a large burst on baseline but not on our dedicated pool tests.
[00:06:18] Carlos Mendes: good. can we get the raw logs?
[00:06:21] Priya Nair: yes, we will share sanitized logs and the profiling exports. Marcus will upload the sheet and logs to the shared folder.
[00:06:28] Aisha Khan: about the model version — are you running the exact same model weights as baseline?
[00:06:33] Marcus Lee: yes we used the same open checkpoint you provided in the spec. quant4 is a post-training quantization we applied — we documented the toolchain in the notes.
[00:06:42] Tom Baker: we need the chain-of-custody for the weights and the quant tool to satisfy audit.
[00:06:47] Priya Nair: will include a short provenance doc and the quant pipeline notes.
[00:06:52] Lena Park: great. last piece — staging plan and timing. goal is to run an end-to-end test in staging next week. Carlos, you said your team can provide replay?
[00:07:01] Carlos Mendes: yes we can produce a 10-minute replay by Monday. we'll also provide staging access for the team to fire real requests.
[00:07:07] Lena Park: ok next steps we'll capture in the follow-up email. any other questions?
[00:07:12] Aisha Khan: small one — can we toggle quant per-route dynamically?
[00:07:15] Marcus Lee: yes our routing supports per-route model variants and automatic fallback, so you can have a float route and quant route and fallback to float on quality checks.
[00:07:24] Maya Li: thanks.
[00:07:26] Carlos Mendes: thanks all.

--- partial middle of call transcript (discussion continued, demos and screensharing) ---

[00:20:05] Marcus Lee: walking through the spreadsheet: you'll see columns for p50/p95/p99, qps, batch window, kernel utilization, and an notes column. for example row 14 is your core QA prompt set where redwood-v1 p99 was 380ms vs baseline 760ms.
[00:20:22] Aisha Khan: i see that, good. row 14 flagged some hallucinations under quant4, which are the ones we noted earlier.
[00:21:00] Marcus Lee: for mitigation we suggested two things: prompt engineering and dynamic model selection (route critical prompts to float). also we can run higher-precision for the first N tokens to anchor outputs.
[00:21:15] Tom Baker: about autoscaling — how quickly can you scale up the dedicated pool? we can't have long cold periods.
[00:21:22] Marcus Lee: scale-up is typically within 45-90 seconds depending on GPU availability in the pool; we recommend warm pools with burst capacity for spikes.
[00:21:33] Carlos Mendes: is there a cost hit for keeping warm pools?
[00:21:36] Lena Park: yes slightly — warm pools incur a minimal standby charge but much cheaper than cold-start latencies for your SLAs. we'll include pricing examples.
[00:21:45] Aisha Khan: one more in the perf area — did you measure tokenization variability? we saw differences in token counts between providers.
[00:21:52] Marcus Lee: we used the same tokenizer config but small differences can happen if whitespace gets normalized differently in the pipeline; we normalized inputs to match your baseline tests.
[00:22:02] Carlos Mendes: ok thanks.

--- closing section ---

[00:38:10] Lena Park: recap: Marcus uploads detailed CSV + logs by Friday (2026-05-01), Centauri provides 10-minute staging replay and access by 2026-05-05, Redwood sends committed pricing delta by 2026-05-03, and we'll schedule the staging run for week of 2026-05-11.
[00:38:30] Carlos Mendes: confirmed.
[00:38:33] Aisha Khan: confirmed.
[00:38:36] Tom Baker: thanks everyone.
[00:38:39] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with an email and the attachments.
[00:38:44] Marcus Lee: thanks.
[00:42:00] call end
